name: Vorelo — Two-Way Job Board
author: matchworkhq

sections.description:
Vorelo is a complete, two-way job board for WordPress. Unlike most job board plugins, both sides are first-class: employers post jobs and can proactively contact candidates, while candidates publish a profile and apply to jobs. It works out of the box — no extra add-ons to buy and no WooCommerce to configure.

Why Vorelo

  • Two-way matching — employers reach out to candidates and candidates apply to jobs. Bidirectional contact is included.
  • All-in-one — job listings, candidate profiles, applications, CV upload, expiry management and essential email notifications in a single plugin.
  • Ready in minutes — pages are created automatically on activation, with roles and taxonomies pre-configured.
  • Your brand, your style — customize colors, fonts, buttons and cards with built-in appearance settings. For more extensive styling, use custom CSS with the included CSS variable and class reference.
  • Your own welcome text — customize the headline and introduction on the “Choose your path” page directly from the settings, without editing plugin files.
  • Ready-made taxonomy terms — start with generic roles, contracts and shifts, then add terms for your industry.
  • Privacy-first — contact details stay hidden until an application is accepted; built-in account deletion for GDPR.

Features

  • Job listings and candidate profiles with search and filters (city, role, contract type, shifts)
  • Bidirectional applications with statuses (sent, seen, accepted, rejected)
  • CV upload and secure, permission-based download
  • Registration and role activation for candidates and employers
  • Candidate and employer dashboards
  • Unlimited saved jobs for candidates, with a dedicated dashboard tab
  • Built-in appearance controls: color palettes, typography, button shapes, card styles, corner radii and spacing
  • Editable headline and introduction for the “Choose your path” welcome page
  • Essential email notifications
  • Basic platform statistics, including traffic and conversion (admin)
  • Generic roles, contracts and shifts seeded on activation

Everything above works out of the box, with no license key and no add-ons to buy.

Quick start

  1. Activate Vorelo and follow the Installation notes below, including CV protection on Nginx.
  2. Add the generated “Choose your path” and “Job listings” pages to your site menu.
  3. In Vorelo → Settings, set your Privacy Policy URL. Add or edit city, role, contract and shift terms in the admin.
  4. Use Appearance for colors, fonts, buttons and cards; its CSS reference covers advanced styling. Use Static messages → Hero for the welcome headline and introduction.
  5. Test with separate candidate and employer accounts: publish a profile and a job, then apply or send a proposal. Manage responses in the dashboards; contact details unlock after acceptance.

Vorelo bundles Choices.js 10.2.0 under the MIT license for accessible multi-select fields. The preferred source and build instructions are available at https://github.com/Choices-js/Choices/tree/v10.2.0.
sections.installation:
1. Upload the plugin to the /wp-content/plugins/vorelo-job-board directory, or install it through the WordPress Plugins screen.
  2. Activate the plugin through the Plugins screen. All required pages are created automatically.
  3. Go to Vorelo → Settings to optionally set your Privacy Policy URL. Add industry-specific taxonomy terms in the admin as needed.
  4. Share the “Choose your path” page so candidates and employers can register.

Nginx users — protect the CV storage. New CVs use wp-content/uploads/vorelo/; existing uploads/matchwork/ vaults stay in place. Downloads use PHP permission and audit checks. Apache uses the plugin’s .htaccess, but Nginx ignores it. Block both paths in your server block (adapt them if your uploads URL differs):

location ^~ /wp-content/uploads/vorelo/ { deny all; return 404; }

location ^~ /wp-content/uploads/matchwork/ { deny all; return 404; }
sections.faq:
Is it really two-way?

Yes. Candidates apply to jobs, and employers can also send contact proposals directly to candidates. Bidirectional contact is included.

Do I need WooCommerce or any add-on?

No. Vorelo works on its own — no add-ons and no WooCommerce required.

Are contact details public?

No. A candidate’s email and phone become visible to an employer only after the application (or proposal) has been accepted, and vice versa. CV downloads are permission-based and every access is logged.

Can I use it for a specific industry?

Yes. Generic roles, contract types and shifts are seeded on activation. Add or edit terms from the admin for your industry.

Does it send any data to the developer?

No. Vorelo bundles no licensing or telemetry SDK and sends no data off your site. For its own features it stores some data locally in your WordPress database — for example job and profile view counts and CV download access logs — which never leaves your server.
sections.changelog:
1.8.2

  • Fix: uninstall works without Enterprise files and removes taxonomy terms even after deactivation.
  • Improvement: new CV vaults use uploads/vorelo; existing uploads/matchwork vaults remain supported without moving files. Nginx instructions cover both paths.
  • Docs: added a quick-start guide. Older changelog entries are preserved in changelog.txt.
  • Release quality: native uninstall bootstrap regression added to the publication workflow; CV browser tests also verify that direct file access is blocked.

1.8.1

  • Improvement: job listings show whether the candidate has applied, received an invitation or already has an accepted relationship; an optional filter hides previously pursued or closed opportunities while keeping unanswered invitations visible.
  • Improvement: employer candidate search shows relationship status and can hide candidates already involved in an application or proposal.
  • Fix: internal agency draft shortlists never appear in participant-facing status badges; withdrawals remain distinct from candidate or employer rejections.
  • Fix: job-card status and save controls wrap correctly on narrow screens.
  • i18n: Italian translations updated for the new status badges and filters.

For earlier releases, see changelog.txt included with the plugin.

upgrade_notice.1.8.2: Fixes Free uninstall and taxonomy cleanup. Existing CV storage stays in place; new vaults use uploads/vorelo. Nginx administrators should block both CV paths as described in Installation. No database migration required.
upgrade_notice.1.8.1: Adds relationship-status badges and optional search filters, with correct invitation, withdrawal and rejection labels and improved mobile card layout. No database migration required.
upgrade_notice.1.8.0: Adds free, unlimited saved jobs for candidates, including dashboard management and privacy-tool integration. No database migration required.
upgrade_notice.1.7.3: Security and privacy fixes: candidate profiles and the recent-jobs shortcode are no longer exposed to anonymous visitors. Recommended for all sites. No database migration required.
upgrade_notice.1.7.1: Documentation and admin screens updated to describe only the features included in this version. No database migration required.

screenshots.caption: Choose your path — candidates and employers each start from a tailored entry point.
Browse jobs with keyword search and filters by city, contract type and shifts — and see at a glance which ones you have already applied to, been invited to, or had accepted.
Open a job to read the details and apply in one step — or save it for later.
The candidate dashboard: manage your profile, applications, proposals and saved jobs.
Saved jobs — bookmark roles and find them again in a dedicated tab.
Candidates receive proposals from employers; once accepted, contact details are revealed.
Post a job in minutes: title, description, location and requirements.
The employer dashboard reviews applications received — candidate surnames stay masked until accepted.
Employers search and reach out to candidates by keyword, city, role, contract and shift, with each candidate's status — in progress, accepted — shown at a glance.
A full candidate profile; email, phone and CV unlock only after an accepted application or proposal.
